body:
Adds `research/speed-race` (MIT, stdlib-only Python, 12 tests, white paper), a README entry and a portfolio page section.

Extends `straggler-backup`, which took worker speeds as given: if the first k of n finishers are paid, speed becomes a contest.

- Win probability is a finite Beta sum; slope at the symmetric point telescopes to `(1-k/n)(H_n-H_{n-k})` (verified numerically, not proved).
- Equilibrium speed is `R(n-k)(H_n-H_{n-k})/(nc)`; exact round time is `nc/((n-k)R)`. Global best response checked on a grid.
- Paying all finishers buys no speed. Under a budget, speed alone wants winner-take-all until an accuracy floor binds. Recruiting more workers barely speeds the round.

Limits are listed in the paper: exponential races, linear cost, symmetric risk-neutral workers, one-shot game.
